parts: The cart has a mass of 12 kilograms.
A balance compares the mass of two objects.
A class places 8 bean seeds in a pot of soil.
Keep the soil moist and record which seeds begin to grow.
A square garden has sides of 6 metres.
Multiply the length by the width to calculate its area.
The experiment uses 25 millilitres of liquid water.
Cooling water enough can change it from a liquid to a solid.
On this map, a line of 3 centimetres represents a road of 15 kilometres.
Use the map scale to compare the lengths of the two routes.
The program repeats an instruction 4 times.
A loop lets the computer follow the same instruction again.
The classroom timeline marks a library opening in 1950.
Place earlier events to the left of later events on the timeline.
Students count 18 birds near a pond during a short survey.
Repeat the survey at the same time of day to make the observations easier to compare.
